cards.question: What process is used to receive transmitted data and convert it into a readable message?

explanation.eli5: For "What process is used to receive transmitted data and convert it into a readable message?", this answer is correct: "decoding". In simple terms, decoding is the process of receiving transmitted data and reversing the encoding process to interpret the information. An example is a person that listens to a voicemail and decodes the sounds to understand the received message.

cards.question: What is done to an IP packet before it is transmitted over the physical medium?
options: It is tagged with information guaranteeing reliable delivery.
It is segmented into smaller individual pieces.
It is encapsulated into a TCP segment.
It is encapsulated in a Layer 2 frame.

answers.text: It is encapsulated in a Layer 2 frame.

explanation.eli5: For "What is done to an IP packet before it is transmitted over the physical medium?", this answer is correct: "It is encapsulated in a Layer 2 frame.". In simple terms, when messages are sent on a network, the encapsulation process works from the top of the OSI or TCP/IP model to the bottom. At each layer of the model, the upper layer information is encapsulated into the data field of the next protocol. For example, before an IP packet can be sent, it is encapsulated in a data link frame at Layer 2 so that it can be sent over the physical medium.

cards.question: A web client is sending a request for a webpage to a web server. From the perspective of the client, what is the correct order of the protocol stack that is used to prepare the request for transmission?

explanation.eli5: For "A web client is sending a request for a webpage to a web server. From the perspective of the client, what is the correct order of the protocol stack that is used to prepare the request for transmission?", this answer is correct: "HTTP, TCP, IP, Ethernet". In simple terms, 1. HTTP governs the way that a web server and client interact. 2. TCP manages individual conversations between web servers and clients. 3. IP is responsible for delivery across the best path to the destination. 4. Ethernet takes the packet from IP and formats it for transmission.

cards.question: What are two benefits of using a layered network model? (Choose two.)
options: It prevents designers from creating their own model.
It prevents technology in one layer from affecting other layers.
It ensures a device at one layer can function at the next higher layer.

explanation.eli5: For "What are two benefits of using a layered network model? (Choose two.)", this choice is correct: "It assists in protocol design.". In simple terms, some vendors have developed their own reference models and protocols. Today, if a device is to communicate on the Internet, the device must use the TCP/IP model. The benefits of using a layered model are as follows: assists in protocol design fosters competition between vendors prevents a technology that functions at one layer from affecting any other layer provides a common language for describing network functionality helps in visualizing the interaction between each layer and protocols between each layer.

cards.question: What is the purpose of protocols in data communications?
options: specifying the bandwidth of the channel or medium for each type of communication
specifying the device operating systems that will support the communication
providing the rules required for a specific type of communication to occur
dictating the content of the message sent during communication

answers.text: providing the rules required for a specific type of communication to occur

explanation.eli5: For "What is the purpose of protocols in data communications?", this answer is correct: "providing the rules required for a specific type of communication to occur". In simple terms, protocols provide rules that define how a message is transmitted across a network. Implementation requirements such as electronic and bandwidth details for data communication are specified by standards. Operating systems are not specified by protocols, but will implement protocols. Protocols determine how and when to send a message but they do not control the contents of a message.

cards.question: Which logical address is used for delivery of data to a remote network?

explanation.eli5: For "Which logical address is used for delivery of data to a remote network?", this answer is correct: "destination IP address". In simple terms, the destination IP address is used for end-to-end delivery of data to a remote network. The destination MAC address is used for delivery on a local network. The destination port number identifies the application that should process the data at the destination. Source addresses identify the sender of the data.

cards.question: What is the general term that is used to describe a piece of data at any layer of a networking model?

explanation.eli5: For "What is the general term that is used to describe a piece of data at any layer of a networking model?", this answer is correct: "protocol data unit". In simple terms, the term protocol data unit (PDU) is used to describe a piece of data at any layer of a networking model. A packet is the PDU at the network layer. A frame is the data link layer PDU. A segment is the PDU at the transport layer.

cards.question: Which layer of the OSI model defines services to segment and reassemble data for individual communications between end devices?

explanation.eli5: For "Which layer of the OSI model defines services to segment and reassemble data for individual communications between end devices?", this answer is correct: "transport". cards.question: Which type of communication will send a message to a group of host destinations simultaneously?

explanation.eli5: For "Which type of communication will send a message to a group of host destinations simultaneously?", this answer is correct: "multicast". In simple terms, multicast is a one-to-many communication where the message is delivered to a specific group of hosts. Broadcast communication is a one-to-all communication. A unicast communication is a one-to-one communication. Anycast is an IPv6 term and is the sending of data in a one-to-nearest communication.

cards.question: In computer communication, what is the purpose of message encoding?
options: to convert information to the appropriate form for transmission
to break large messages into smaller frames
negotiate correct timing for successful communication

answers.text: to convert information to the appropriate form for transmission

explanation.eli5: For "In computer communication, what is the purpose of message encoding?", this answer is correct: "to convert information to the appropriate form for transmission". In simple terms, before a message is sent across a network it must first be encoded. Encoding is the process of converting the data message into another format suitable for transmission across the physical medium. Each bit of the message is encoded into a pattern of sounds, light waves, or electrical impulses depending on the network media over which the bits are transmitted. The destination host receives and decodes the signals in order to interpret the message.

cards.question: Which message delivery option is used when all devices need to receive the same message simultaneously?

explanation.eli5: For "Which message delivery option is used when all devices need to receive the same message simultaneously?", this answer is correct: "broadcast". In simple terms, when all devices need to receive the same message simultaneously, the message would be delivered as a broadcast. Unicast delivery occurs when one source host sends a message to one destination host. The sending of the same message from a host to a group of destination hosts is multicast delivery. Duplex communications refers to the ability of the medium to carry messages in both directions.
